failure_scenario: On a common 360 px Android phone the first screen of the import flow scrolls horizontally, and the help link's text runs past the card border.
fix: Make it a short button ('Slow-motion help') after a one-line sentence, or render it as an inline text link that can wrap (no whitespace-nowrap).

title: Live framing at 200% text: the prompt covers the checklist, check names truncate and the ready pill overflows
detail: The camera overlay mixes fixed-height pills (h-11 '2 of 9 ready') and a fixed-size checklist panel with rem text. At 200% the 'Turn the phone upright' prompt and its detail card sit on top of the Checks panel, the check names truncate ('Le…', 'In fr…', 'Ro…'), and '2 of 9 ready' spills outside its pill border. At 390 without enlarged text, the prompt's detail card already overlaps the 'Toss room above' guide label. Evidence: states/live-390-light-200-framing.png, states/live-390-light-framing.png.
failure_scenario: A player who uses larger text sets up the phone at the fence. They cannot read which of the 9 checks still needs a fix because the names are cut off and hidden under the prompt.
fix: Use min-h on the ready pill. Stack the prompt and the checklist in one flow column so they cannot overlap, and at large text sizes show the checklist as a single-column list rather than a 3-column grid of truncated names.

title: The service-box chart's 'Net' label is drawn outside the SVG over the caption, and zone labels collide at large text
detail: HEIGHT is 300, but the Net label is placed at netY + STRIP + 14 = 329, and PlotSurface sets overflow-visible, so 'Net' prints over 'Schematic: each mark is a serve you logged…' on every report at every width and theme. The SVG geometry is fixed px while <text> uses rem caption/headline sizes. In Court-side (heavier weight), and at 150 to 200%, the zone labels and counts collide ('WideWideBody', '5 3 5' on the labels). The wide-fault count '2' also sits under the net line, where it reads as a net count. Evidence: slices/390-light-report-s3-03.png, slices/390-light-200-report-s3-06.png.
failure_scenario: Every player who opens a session report sees 'Net' printed on top of the caption under the Outcomes chart. At large text the zone names are unreadable.
fix: Include the Net strip label in the height (HEIGHT = netY + STRIP + 22, or compute it from font metrics). Clip or measure text with the rendered font size, put counts on their own row above the zone names, and move the wide count next to the Wide strip label.

title: The likely-range bars on 'Did it work?' are nearly invisible in Court-side (sun) and Night modes
detail: The 95% and 80% interval bars use fillOpacity 0.12 and 0.22 of the series colour. On the surface that is about 1.1 to 1.3:1, well under the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 and DESIGN §12 require for chart marks. Court-side doesn't strengthen them. In Night the 'Before' bar is a faint grey smear. These bars are the uncertainty the verdict rests on ('darker is 80%, lighter is 95%'). Evidence: slices/390-court-compare-00.png, slices/390-dark-compare-00.png.
failure_scenario: On court at midday a player opens 'Did it work?'. They see only two tick marks and cannot tell that the before and after ranges overlap or how wide they are, so the 'Clearly better' verdict looks more certain than it is.
fix: Draw each interval with a ≥3:1 outline (stroke in the series colour, or line-strong) and use solid fills with ≥3:1 between the 80% and 95% tones in Court-side, or use a hatch for 95%. Add these pairs to tokens.test contrast checks.

title: The Sessions list cuts off the 'early read' qualifier at default size and the serve count at large text
detail: ListRow's subtitle is 'truncate' (one line) and its detail is 'line-clamp-2'. The sample check-in headline '14 of 16 serves measured. Toss height varied by about 30 cm (early read).' is clamped to '…about 30 cm…' at 390 px default text, so the provisional qualifier disappears. At 200% the subtitle becomes 'Side view · 16 …', which drops 'of 16 measured'. DESIGN §12 says no truncation of values, and the honesty rules require n and state on every number. Evidence: 390-light-sessions.png, slices/390-light-200-sessions-00.png.
failure_scenario: A player scanning the Sessions list reads 'Toss height varied by about 30 cm' as a settled result, because '(early read)' was cut. At large text they can't see how many serves were measured.
fix: Let subtitle and detail wrap in session rows (no truncate or line-clamp), or put the qualifier first ('Early read: toss height varied…'). Keep values and n out of truncated spans.

title: Serve detail scrolls 16 px sideways at 320 px: a class conflict makes the prev/next buttons 48 px
detail: The Previous serve, Next serve and ±10 frame buttons use cx(BTN, 'size-11'), but BTN already contains size-12. In the built CSS .size-12 comes after .size-11, so they render at 48 px. The right slot (w-24, 96 px) must hold 48+4+48 = 100 px. At 320x640 'Next serve' ends at x=336 and the document overflows by 16 px, against DESIGN §12 (reflow at 320 without horizontal scroll). At 390 the slot already overflows into the gap next to 'Forward 1 frame'. Evidence: 320-light-serve-detail.png, summary-320-and-150pct.json.
failure_scenario: On an iPhone SE-class or other 320 px screen, the Next serve control sits partly off-screen and the whole serve detail page pans sideways when swiped.
fix: Remove size-12 from BTN and set the size per button (or use tailwind-merge in cx). Let the side slots be flex-1 min-w-0 instead of a fixed w-24.

title: Serve detail and Tagging nest a second <main> inside the shell's <main id='main'>
detail: AppShell already renders <main id='main'>. ServeDetailScreen (line 518), CheckServeView (line 419) and TaggingScreen (lines 217 and 481) render their own <main>. axe reports landmark-main-is-top-level, landmark-no-duplicate-main and landmark-unique on every run of serve-detail and tagging (16 of 16 configs).
failure_scenario: A VoiceOver rotor user jumping to 'main' lands on two unnamed main landmarks and the skip link target is ambiguous.
fix: Change the inner <main> elements to <div> (or <section aria-label=…>) and keep the shell's main as the single landmark.

title: Headings jump from h1 to h3 on the check-in report and on 'Did it work?'
detail: axe heading-order fails on /sessions/sample-s2 (the FocusCard title 'Steady toss height' is an h3 with no h2 before it) and on /progress/compare (ChartFrame defaults to headingLevel h3, used at CompareScreen.tsx line 116 directly after the h1). It fails in all 16 base configs.
failure_scenario: A screen-reader user navigating by heading level misses these sections when listing h2s and hears a skipped level.
fix: Pass headingLevel='h2' to ChartFrame on CompareScreen. Let FocusCard take a heading level, or put it under an h2 section label on the report.

title: Closing the expanded drawer with Escape drops keyboard focus to <body>
detail: The drawer's Escape handler only calls onExpandedChange(false). If focus was inside the drawer body (for example a key-frame 'Peak. Show this frame' button), that body becomes hidden and focus falls to document.body. The next Tab restarts at 'Skip to content'. Verified in states/390-light-*: after 25 Tabs plus Escape, activeElement is BODY.
failure_scenario: A keyboard user opens 'All values', moves into the key frames, presses Escape, and loses their place on the page.
fix: On Escape (and on the 'Show less' toggle), move focus back to the 'All values' button whenever activeElement is inside the drawer body.

title: Several targets are under 44 x 44 px: target chips, the tagging Let/Skip buttons and the height field
detail: The chip hit area is 'after:inset-x-0 after:-inset-y-1', so only height is extended. The 'T' chip is 39x44 on Tagging and 31x44 in Record's target row, and the 'Ad' segment is 41x44. The tertiary Let (31x44) and Skip (41x44) buttons on the tagging pad are also short. In HeightInput (parts/HeightInput.tsx line 127) the real <input> is only 26 px tall inside a 52 px box that is not a label, which leaves dead zones above and below the digits. DESIGN §12 and §14 require at least 44x44 on every target.
failure_scenario: Tagging at the fence between serves, a player aims for 'T' or 'Let' with a thumb and misses because the target is 31 px wide.
fix: Add min-w-11 to chips and tertiary pad buttons (or after:-inset-x-[n] as needed). Make the height box a <label htmlFor> or give the input h-full.

title: In Night mode, inactive tab labels fall below 4.5:1 over the glass tab bar
detail: Inactive labels are text-ink-3 (#8d978f) at 12 px on the translucent .glass bar. On Log practice in Night, with the selected (light) chip scrolled under the bar, axe measured 4.26:1 against the blended #2e332f background. Contrast depends on the content behind the bar, and DESIGN asks for AAA on secondary text.
failure_scenario: A night-comp player on Log practice in dark mode can't reliably read 'Today' or 'Record' in the tab bar while lighter content scrolls beneath it.
fix: Use text-ink-2 for inactive tab labels, or make the bar background opaque enough (for example 96%) that the worst case stays at or above 4.5:1. Add the pair to tokens.test.

title: The phase timeline disappears in forced-colours (Windows High Contrast) mode
detail: Phase spans are background-only divs (bg-ink-3, bg-surface-2, bg-band) with no border or forced-colors rule. Under forced-colors: active their backgrounds are removed, so the serve timeline shows only stray tick glyphs and the playhead ring. The focus-phase highlight is gone too. DESIGN §12 requires marks to use system colours in forced colours. Evidence: states/forced-serve.png.
failure_scenario: A Windows High Contrast user reviewing a serve on a laptop can't see where Toss, Loading or Contact phases are on the scrubber.
fix: Give spans a 1 px border (forced-color-adjust: none, or a @media (forced-colors: active) rule using CanvasText/Highlight), and draw the focus phase with Highlight.

title: Interactive charts are exposed as role='img', so arrow-key selection is hidden from screen readers
detail: The plot SVG has role='img', aria-label and tabIndex=0, and handles Arrow, Enter and Escape to select and open serves. role='img' makes the children presentational, and screen readers in browse mode don't pass arrow keys to an image. The selection only surfaces through the sr-only live region, and nothing tells the user the chart is operable.
failure_scenario: A VoiceOver user reaches the toss beeswarm, hears 'Peak height of each serve, 16 serves, image', and never learns they can arrow through serves or press Enter to open one.
fix: Use role='application' (or role='group' with aria-roledescription='chart') on the interactive surface and add usage to the label or aria-describedby ('Use arrow keys to move between serves, Enter to open'). Keep role='img' only for non-interactive plots.

title: A missing video shows 'Couldn't see this clearly' with the skeleton drawn over the message
detail: When video.storage is 'idb' but the blob can't be loaded (videoUrl null) and there are no stills, goneLine is null. The placeholder then falls back to REASON_FALLBACK 'Couldn't see this clearly', which is a pose-quality reason, not a missing-video state. VideoStage still receives scene (line 529), so the overlay canvas paints the skeleton on top of the icon and text. This was reproduced when IndexedDB video blobs were absent (a restored storage state without blobs).
failure_scenario: After a recording whose chunks were never assembled, or a partial restore, the player sees a skeleton over 'Couldn't see this clearly' and thinks the pose failed, when the video is simply missing.
fix: When hasVideo and stepping are both false, use an explicit line such as 'This video isn't on this phone. Phases and values are below.' and pass scene={null} so no overlay paints over the placeholder.

title: The Sessions list shows capture quality as a glyph only, with the word visible only to screen readers
detail: CaptureGlyph renders a check-circle or warning glyph with the word in sr-only text. DESIGN §12 requires glyph + word for capture quality, and D2 now also requires the experimental label. Sighted users see an unlabelled tick next to every row, which reads as 'done' or 'verified'.
failure_scenario: A player scanning the Sessions list reads the tick as 'this session is verified'. They can't tell Good from Fair without opening each report.
fix: Show a compact visible word ('Good', 'Fair', 'Limited') next to the glyph, or drop the glyph from the row and rely on the report's full capture line (with its experimental label).

title: The dev component gallery ships in production at /dev/components
detail: The route table registers 'dev/components' with no import.meta.env.DEV guard. In the production build it renders the full gallery: token swatches, fixture values and working Theme/Court-side controls that write the persisted theme setting. The data README says hand-authored fixtures are for tests and development only.
failure_scenario: A beta tester who follows a shared link or guesses the URL sees fixture numbers that look like real metrics and can change their saved theme from a developer page.
fix: Register the route only when import.meta.env.DEV is true (or behind the beta/dev flag), so the lazy chunk is excluded from production.

title: The processing route's title says 'Analysing' after analysis has finished
detail: The route handle title for processing/:sessionId is always 'Analysing'. Opening it for a finished session shows the app bar 'Analysing' above 'This session is analysed. Your report is ready.' The document title says Analysing too. Evidence: 390-light-processing.png.
failure_scenario: A player who returns from a notification or a Sessions row sees a header that says the app is still analysing, directly above a message saying it's done.
fix: Let ProcessingScreen set the title from the session status ('Analysing', 'Report ready', 'Couldn't analyse'), or use a neutral route title such as 'Session'.
